set.rationale: Resolved by later vintages now in the database: SIA's own 2026 State of the Industry report replaced its February 2026 US$791.7bn with WSTS's US$795.6bn (CLM-2306), and WSTS's final 2025 figure is US$795.6bn (CLM-2316). Gartner's preliminary US$793bn was superseded by US$805.3bn (April) and US$809.0bn (August 2026, CLM-2308), which measure a different, modelled population (see CON-0015, definitional).

Reclassified: comparable is false. WSTS (member-reported product sales, US$630.5bn) and Gartner (modelled vendor revenue, final US$655.9bn) measure different populations; Gartner's preliminary US$626bn is simply superseded by its own final figure. Same finding as CON-0016 (definitional).
Same publisher, later vintage: Gartner's April 2025 table restates Nvidia's 2023 revenue at US$34.8bn, replacing the January 2024 preliminary ~US$24bn; the restatement is Gartner's current view.

Same publisher, later vintage: WSTS's July 2026 calculation (US$1,655bn) replaces the June 2026 forecast (US$1.51tn) because it incorporates actual Q2 2026 data. Cross-publisher 2026 forecasts are recorded separately as definitional.

Both estimates (Oct 2024: 140-150k; Dec 2025: 120-130k wafers/month) are superseded by 2026-vintage estimates of 115-140k for end-2026 (CLM-1264, CLM-1265, CLM-1587, CLM-1588, CLM-1589), which cluster around the later Dec 2025 range. The remaining spread among 2026 estimates is tracked in CON-0052.

Not a live conflict: TrendForce's 30% was a May 2024 projection; Gartner's 23% (with HBM above US$30bn) is a post-year estimate of 2025. A later TrendForce release (June 2026) gives HBM about 18% of DRAM wafer input and 8% of bit supply at end-2025, consistent with a value share in the low-20s rather than above 30%.

Resolved by CLM-1274 and CLM-1218 (verified): the 'near 50%' cut referred to wafer fab equipment capex and was already decided before November 2022; Micron's total net capex fell about 41.5% (US$11.98bn in FY2022 to US$7.01bn in FY2023, our arithmetic in CLM-1274). Both statements are correct for their own scope.

CLM-1072 has been superseded by CLM-1235, which no longer counts HCL-Foxconn Jewar as a pure wafer fab; TechCrunch (CLM-1234) and the IESA president's statement at approval (CLM-1275) both describe the unit as initially an OSAT.

CLM-0561 was refuted by fact-check and superseded by CLM-2349; CLM-1343 (verified, high) reads automotive 12.7% and consumer 9.9% for 2024, confirmed by SIA SOI 2026 (2024: automotive 13%, consumer 10%).

CLM-1289 (verified, high) quotes the WSTS 2021 Product Classification, section 3.2 (F6): 'Other Optoelectronics ... including fiber optic components and solar cells'. The earlier unknown (CLM-0016) reflected a failed text search, not absence.

The SIA-vs-WSTS gap is closed: SIA's 2026 State of the Industry report revised 2025 memory to US$230.0bn (CLM-2307), matching WSTS (CLM-0036, CLM-2320). The remaining WSTS (US$230.0bn) vs Gartner (US$216.3bn April, US$220.1bn August) gap is between different populations (member-reported sales vs modelled vendor revenue), as for the total market in CON-0015.

Resolved on the primary texts: MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 70 suspended only Nos. 55-58, 61 and 62 (CLM-1396, verified high) and does not list the April 2025 rare-earth controls (No. 18), which remain in force (CLM-1397, verified). The White House's 'de facto removal' (CLM-1398) described intended general licences; its later fact sheets (CLM-1401, CLM-1402) confirm shortages persisted into September 2026.

Nikkei's 2025 market-share survey puts Shin-Etsu at 26.3% and SUMCO at 17.8% (44.1% combined), with the 3rd-5th makers (Taiwan, Germany, Korea) at 31.9%. This is incompatible with ITA's unsourced 'about 90%' for the two Japanese firms (the 90% figure matches the top five suppliers, not two) and close to the Brookings 53% for Japan (CLM-1825). Brookings' attributed figure is more defensible.

Still open, but narrowed: Nikkei's 2025 survey puts the three largest photoresist makers, all Japanese (TOK, JSR, Shin-Etsu), at 60.5% combined, and TOK alone at 26.1% (CLM-1826, Fuji Chimera). Japanese firms' total share is therefore above 60%, which makes the Brookings 50% look low and the ITA/USITC 90% look high unless it counts production in Japan or specific resist types (EUV/ArF).

SEMI's July 2026 release implies a 2025 A&P actual of about US$6.11bn (US$6.7bn / 1.096) and a 2024 base of about US$5.06bn (6.11 / 1.208). The December 2025 forecast's +19.6% implies a 2024 base of US$5.02bn for the US$6.0bn version and US$5.35bn for US$6.4bn (our arithmetic). Only the semi.org figure (US$6.0bn) is consistent with SEMI's own series; US$6.4bn is most likely a typo in the PR Newswire copy.

The 86.5% was a planned stake in TSMC's February 2024 announcement. TSMC's 2025 annual report shows 73% at end-2025 (CLM-2117, verified high) and its FY2025 Form 20-F says about 72.6% as of 28 February 2026 (CLM-2324): the same figure rounded. The audited-period disclosures supersede the plan.

Reclassified: comparable is false. CSIS's 'up to one-third of capital costs' describes a general programme rule, while DIGITIMES's 40% divides JASM's two maximum subsidies (¥1.208tn) by TSMC's stated >US$20bn investment, a different denominator converted at an unstated exchange rate.

Reclassified: comparable is false. The TWSE ISIN register counts classified listed stocks (91), while the MOPS monthly revenue table lists companies that filed revenue in that section (88); the populations differ by construction.

Arithmetic on Deloitte's own endnotes (about 20 million AI chips / 1.05 trillion chips = 0.0019%) was independently verified (CLM-2265). Deloitte's '0.2%' is off by a factor of 100 unless it used an undisclosed denominator.

Reclassified: comparable is false. IC Knowledge's 17% includes a 10-point penalty for a smaller, unclustered fab; its same-size country difference (7%) agrees with TechInsights' 'less than 10%' for the same wafer. The figures answer different questions.

CLM-0345 (USITC briefing citing press reports) was marked outdated by fact-check; USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (CLM-2249, verified high, official statistics) gives China 99% of world primary low-purity gallium production.

Same finding as CON-0084 (resolved): the fact-checks of CLM-0477 and CLM-0412 confirm that the report's sidebar and Exhibit 4 give design 50% of value added and that only those shares sum to 100%; the 53% in the running text is the design share of R&D.

Reclassified: these are forecasts by different publishers on different populations and vintages (WSTS member-reported memory sales, June 2026; Gartner modelled vendor revenue, April and August 2026). Within each publisher the later vintage supersedes the earlier; across publishers no figure can be preferred until 2026 actuals. See the new 2026 total-market forecast entry in this batch.

Ledger duplicate: the same disagreement (Besi end-2025 hybrid-bonding customers: 18 in the FY2025 release vs 15 in the H1-26 release) is tracked in CON-0073, which also includes the Q1-26 count. The Q2-26 wording 'from 15 at year end 2025 to 21' is confirmed in Besi's H1-26 release; the conflict remains open in CON-0073.
